what: Text box (data-fx-part=glyph) are redrawn on a WebGL plate so they look like islands submerged in water — bold characters (data-key=Bold text always sits above the water, while thin text is carved away at the noise wave crests (horizontal .5×aspect ratio, vertical .5, flowing at time ×.00012 and rippling at ×.0003, edge noise doubled at ×.0005). On first open the thin text is submerged, then rises after 1.5s over 1s (power1.out). Raising --fx-tide-thin from 0 to 1 adds .28 of waterline and submerges the thin text entirely. --fx-tide-wave (0–1, original .8) lays a dark wave shadow over the whole panel. The waves trail the scroll by .1 per 1/60s and flow backwards. If a box is moved with GSAP, it is redrawn in that spot.

options.depth: Depth of the thin text (opacity painted on the plate) 0~1, default .58 — lower sinks in more easily
options.--fx-tide-thin: Tide level (via style or GSAP) 0–1 — at 1 the thin letters are fully submerged and only bold letters remain
options.--fx-tide-wave: Wave shadow strength (via style or GSAP) 0~1, original About section .8
options.--fx-tide-shade: Shade color (css variable) — if none, the text color dropped to brightness 0 black

use: AR…
note: Letter shape, weight, size and position are read straight from the span’s css and drawn — thin letters should be around font-weight 100 and bold ones around 800, so only the thin side gets shaved like the original. The panel is a canvas the size of the attached element, so for a screen-fixed panel set the element to position: fixed.

from.where: index.html .pl-logo — original canvas#logo (27 letter images painted on a 2D board with a three shader for wave erosion), scatter·gather positions follow the original table in index.js
